newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan shares end higher for 3rd record in row.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan shares end higher for 3rd record in row.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed slightly higher Wednesday, setting a third consecutive record in busy trading, brokers said.
The 19-share index closed up 0.54 percent at 4,738.11, according to figures released by the exchange.
A total of 20 stocks closed higher, 17 lower and five unchanged, reflecting a mixed session in which profit-taking was marginally overshadowed by demand from foriegn buyers, brokers said.
"There is still interest from foreign investors. The market is still strong," said Gabriel Osio of the Amerival brokerage.
Osio pointed out that trading of benchmark Electricidad de Caracas was brisk, with about 3.5 million shares changing hands.
All told, 2.7 billion bolivars ($5.7 million) worth of shares were traded.

Among leading stocks, Electricidad closed up 5.45 bolivars at 407.00 bolivars, cement company Vencemos type 2 shares rose 30.00 bolivars to 870.00 bolivars and agro-industrial company Mavesa slipped 5.50 bolivars to 123.50 bolivars.
Brokers said profit-taking started to kick in after a strong start, suggesting that share prices could slip from record levels on Thursday.
